allocation: valid_i is a packed oldest prefix. A lane-zero CFI terminates the selected prefix. The complete selected prefix must fit the pre-cycle ROB credits, PRF pool and checkpoint bank, with resources_ready_i confirming all downstream reservations. No retirement-credit bypass or lane-zero fallback for a two-instruction resource shortage is implemented. allocate_accept_o alone authorizes downstream dispatch. The caller enforces decode-known serialization barriers.
completion: Two upstream-arbitrated candidates supply held ROB identities and full event records. The wrapper obtains destination tags from ROB ownership, validates generations and the recovery cut, and shares acceptance across ROB completion, PRF writes and readiness. wb_accept_o is the wakeup/bypass mask; complete_accept_o also acknowledges traps and resultless operations that perform no PRF write. PRF payload comes from the accepted event's rd_value. A duplicate offered ROB identity reserves lane zero. Reset, full flush, accepted traps and killed/obsolete packets never write or wake up. Rejected canceled packets must be discarded by the future producer cancellation path; acceptance is not a cancellation acknowledgement.
resolution: resolve_grant_i represents permission from the future oldest-event recovery arbiter. A live unresolved ROB identity selects its internally recorded checkpoint slot. Only shared ROB/checkpoint resolution acceptance may release or restore that checkpoint. Producers do not supply checkpoint IDs. CFI allocation records the slot chosen by the same accepted rename transaction. A misprediction preserves the branch/link and older results, suppresses allocation/retirement and kills younger completions in the winning cycle.
retirement: retire_valid_o exposes an eligible oldest ROB prefix. retire_ready_i represents joint event-sink and architectural-side-effect readiness; slot one cannot retire without slot zero. retire_accept_o is shared with committed-map updates and stale-tag release. Event valid fields describe offered records, not acceptance; consumers act only on the acceptance mask. trap_ready_i authorizes the separate head trap boundary and must be qualified by the future CSR/event controller. trap_accept_o flushes the ROB and restores pre-cycle committed rename state without destination commit. Event order is supplied by the ROB.
reads: read_address_i supplies four physical source tags for the future issue stage. read_ready_o includes same-cycle accepted writes and masks reclaimed tags and global recovery. read_data_o bypasses exactly wb_accept_o; it remains an unqualified physical read when readiness is false. p0 always reads zero. Other PRF payloads are unspecified until written and are not reset. source_ready_o describes the accepted rename bundle including lane-zero RAW/WAW bypass and current accepted writebacks.
drain: drained_i retains the ROB's empty-window/global-producer-quiescence contract. It requires no offered rename, completion or resolution traffic and confirmation that every external holder discarded previous identities. Generation exhaustion is signaled by identity_drain_o. The wrapper does not implement producer cancellation, drain collection or age arbitration. Reset must reset external holders too.
scope: Connected 64-entry PRF, two-wide rename/checkpoint ownership and 32-entry ROB, driven by synthetic dispatch/completion inputs. No IQ, issue selection, execution units, frontend, CSR/MMIO head state machine, physical timing or complete OOO processor acceptance. Commit-only operations require a future atomic head-result/retirement path and trap event finalization; solo flags alone do not implement those operations. This gate is full-size simulation, independent mutation testing and generic synthesis, not an integrated formal proof.
